guard: the delivery daemon is launched with the transport its mesh requires (#836), and a launch that never took the lease is reported as the failure it is rather than as a healthy control plane (#837)
why: BOTH DEFECTS LOOK HEALTHY FROM THE OUTSIDE, which is why the assertions are on the LAUNCH and on
the EXIT CODE rather than on anything the daemon reports about itself. A daemon started without
`--tls` against a TLS broker still connects - it upgrades on the server's unauthenticated INFO -
so no readiness check can distinguish it from a correctly launched one. M1 therefore reddens an
assertion about the ARGV the launcher passed.
M2 AND M3 ARE THE TWO HALVES OF ONE ANSWER, and each is load-bearing on its own. M2 restores the
unscoped wait: readiness is then satisfied by the OTHER daemon's ready lease, so the launch reads
as a slow start that finished. M3 leaves the wait scoped but restores the silent return: the wait
correctly fails and the caller reports success anyway. Either one alone re-opens #837, so both
must redden the same assertion - the exit code of a refresh whose child is already dead.
M2/M3 RUN THE CLI AS A SUBPROCESS, so they mutate a module that only `dist/` delivers to it:
`@cotal-ai/cli` resolves to its build. Every mutation here builds first and rebuilds in
`afterRestore` - `dist/` is gitignored, so git cannot be the recovery for a tree left holding a
build compiled from the mutant.
ONLY M1 DECLARES A `completionMarker`. Its suite prints the per-route table pass or fail, so a
run that never reaches it died of something other than the route. `up-stack` is fail-fast (its
`ok` throws), so it has no line common to both outcomes and declaring one would grade every
genuine kill INCONCLUSIVE.
M3 DISABLES ITS BRANCH WITH A TRAILING `&& false`, AND BOTH OTHER SHAPES WERE MEASURED FIRST.
Prefixing the condition with `false &&` stops TypeScript narrowing `launched` for the `probe(launched)`
call two operands later: the build failed with TS2345 and the run graded WRONG-RED at ZERO marks,
having never reached the suite - a mutation that cannot compile grades the compiler. Asking the probe
for "alive" instead compiles, and is worse: the guard then fires on a daemon that is merely SLOW, so
the mutant reddened an EARLIER assertion in the healthy first `up --detach` and graded WRONG-RED at 8
marks. Only the trailing `&& false` leaves narrowing and every healthy path intact and removes exactly
the refusal under test - which is why the anchor is the condition alone rather than the two-line
condition-plus-throw the first version used.

mutations.name: M1 the delivery launcher re-derives the transport from the broker policy instead of taking the caller's decision (#836)
mutations.find: await ensureControlPlane({ space, server, tls: tlsRequired, ...(mgr ?? {}) });
mutations.replace:
void tlsRequired;
    await ensureControlPlane({ space, server, tls: readBrokerPolicy(cotalRoot())?.transport.kind === "tls-required", ...(mgr ?? {}) });
mutations.expectRed: GATE FAILED (S11/#836): refresh relaunched delivery WITHOUT --tls against a TLS-required broker
mutations.note: The exact shape that shipped: the caller's decision present and unused, the callee consulting a SECOND durable record. A root that records tlsRequired in the mesh registry without a broker-policy file - which is what the S11 route builds, and what a refresh of an adopted mesh looks like - then launches the daemon flagless. `void tlsRequired` keeps the parameter used so the mutant compiles; a mutation that cannot build grades the compiler, not the suite.

mutations.name: M2 the readiness wait stops naming the daemon it launched, so another daemon's ready lease answers for it (#837)
mutations.expectRed: a refresh whose delivery launch loses the single-flight lease exits non-zero
mutations.note: The false-green as it reached operators: `up` exits 0 and prints a healthy control plane while the daemon it started has already exited on a lost CAS, leaving a pidfile that fronts a dead pid.

mutations.name: M3 a launch that is provably dead is reported as a slow start instead of a failure (#837)
mutations.expectRed: a refresh whose delivery launch loses the single-flight lease exits non-zero
mutations.note: The scoped wait alone is not enough: it returns false, the caller prints a note about a daemon that will be ready shortly, and returns running:true for a process that is gone. `probe(launched) === "dead"` is what separates a slow start from a dead one, and only a launch WE performed is ours to judge.
